newsitem.title: UK: Dlr reclaims some ground, closes higher in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dlr reclaims some ground, closes higher in Europe.

text.p: The dollar inched higher in Europe against the mark and the yen in subdued trade as the market searched for impetus beforeFederal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday.
Dealers said the dollar's ability to stay above overnight lows of 1.6670 marks and 121.50 yen was supportive even though in the short-term, the dollar's tone is slightly negative.

"Nagging EMU doubts, rising save-haven demand for marks, the approach of Japan's financial year-end and the abundance of stale dollar longs are all combining to put the dollar into a temporary stall right now," said David Brown at Bear Stearns.

Brown, chief economist at Bear Stearns, said in the short-term it was likely that the dollar would languish, with possible drops below 1.65 and 120 looming on the downside if key stops were taken out. At 1608 GMT the dollar was at 1.6755/60 marks and 122.01/06, up from 1.6690/6700 and 121.88/98 in late Europe on Monday.
Volatility was low ahead of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, starting on Wednesday.
"The dollar is entrenched in a 1.67 to 1.68 mark range, and against the yen it's basically stuck as well after failing to overcome 122.40," said a senior trader at a German bank here.
U.S. data had scant impact on the dollar. The consumer confidence index slipped to 118.4 in February from a revised 118.7 in January but was above 116.1 forecast.
U.S. import prices dropped 0.3 percent in January after a rise of 0.1 percent in December, while export prices were up 0.2 percent after being flat in the previous month.

The mark firmed against the lira amid nervousness ahead of the Italian confidence vote about the government's 1997 budget measures. As expected the government won, which lent some support to the lira. But comments later by Prime Minister Romano Prodi put the lira under renewed pressure.

The dollar got a slight boost in late trade from a comment by European monetary affairs commissioner Yves Thibault de Silguy. He said the dollar's recent rise could be positive for growth in the EU this year.

De Silguy said the EU commission could confirm its earlier prediction that growth in the 15-nation bloc would be 2.3 percent this year, and that the dollar's rise of more than 10 percent above the average for 1996 constituted a positive factor which could result in raising the 1997 growth forecast.
The dollar's surge was cited as having pushed German import prices up 1.0 percent in January from the previous month.

German import prices were up 2.6 percent on the year. The jump in import prices did not feed through into the consumer price index though. Preliminary data for February showed a rise of 0.4 percent on the month and a year-on-year increase of 2.6 percent, in line with forecasts.
The lira came under pressure amid nervousness ahead of a confidence vote about the Italian government's 1997 budget measures. The lira rose as the government won, as expected.
But the lira erased most of its gains against the mark amid late selling of Italian bond futures and after comments by Prime Minister Romano Prodi.
Prodi said in an interview with German weekly newspaper Die Zeit that "great efforts" were necessary for Italy to meet the Maastricht criteria.
Mark/lira was at 995.30/70 in late trade, off its session peak at 995.75 seen prior to the confidence vote but above late Monday's 991.80/992.15.
The Bank of Italy was seen selling marks for lire in midday trade at around 995.50, dealers said. -- Astrid Zweynert London newsroom + 44 171 542 7792
